**A7 adopted parameter record · adopted 20 October 2026 · record `e234e860…` · Engine `8298c602` · [Download exact parameters](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json)**

These are electrolyte PC-SAFT (ePC-SAFT) parameters for aqueous MEA–CO₂, with nine liquid species (CO₂, MEA, H₂O, MEAH⁺, MEACOO⁻, HCO₃⁻, CO₃²⁻, H₃O⁺, OH⁻) and five reactions R1–R5. A7 is the seventh amendment of the joint-recalibration plan in [#170](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170); it is the record adopted on 20 October 2026.

# Adopted record and result {#working-record}

The adopted A7 record fits 16 adjustable parameters to 307 objective rows, using native equation-of-state densities without empirical volume translation. For the common calibration subset, average absolute relative deviations are 11.86% for 47 pressures and 7.10% for 94 species targets; the eight fitted Vinjarapu heats have a root-mean-square error of 1.83 kJ/mol CO₂. Of 47 fitted loaded densities, 44 meet their row-specific limits, with three disclosed failures at 353.15 K; one of four heat-capacity points exceeds the 3% comparison limit. At 73 tested states (313.15–333.15 K, CO₂ loading $10^{-5}$–0.5), the phase-stability search found no phase split with lower Gibbs energy; this finite test does not establish global phase stability. The record is approved for manuscript use, but its single-start local fits, active bounds and conditional uncertainty do not establish parameter uniqueness, independent physical validation, concentration transfer or absorber/stripper qualification.

# Parameters {#selected-parameters}

These tables read the [selected JSON](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json), [fit summary](results/a7-paper-evidence/fit-summary.json), and [conditional uncertainty](results/a7-paper-evidence/conditional-uncertainty.json). Parameter point estimates use about four significant figures; conditional standard errors use two. Hover over starred fitted estimates to see their full-precision values. Full precision remains in the linked JSON and CSV records. The [input hashes](figures/a7_regression_overview/output/parameter-table-inputs.json) identify the inputs.

[Green: a fixed charge or formulation definition]{.evidence-1} · [Blue: a numerical input with recorded qualifications]{.evidence-2}. [★](#fitted-coordinates){.fit-star} identifies fitted component or pair inputs and all 16 declared coordinates. Tied diameters and transformed chemistry are described explicitly. Green does not certify fitted properties.

CO₂ has induced 2B association with water and no self-association; its cross-association inputs are in `topology.edges` of the selected file. Ion association is absent.


::: {title="Exact water-diameter constant 2.78043261494 Å; full coefficients in the selected JSON"}

Water diameter (rounded display; use the selected JSON for numerical work), with $T$ in K and $\sigma$ in Å. The constant and amplitudes are in Å; exponent coefficients are in K⁻¹:

$$\sigma_{\mathrm{H_2O}}(T)=2.78+10.11 e^{-0.01775T}-1.417 e^{-0.01146T}$$

:::

The selected file uses solvent-density-temperature permittivity with the retained shared stage-5 water parameters. It excludes dispersion between ions with the same charge sign. For MEAH⁺ and MEACOO⁻, packing diameter is 0.88 times segment diameter and Debye–Hückel diameter equals segment diameter; Born diameters vary separately. No empirical density translation is applied. Fixed and transferred inputs carry their recorded qualifications; these tables confer no new physical validation.

R5 A is the unshifted source coordinate; enthalpy shifts are totals including inherited shifts. The errors condition on residual weights, fixed inputs, active bounds and local linearization. They do not establish independent-error measurement uncertainty, parameter uniqueness or prediction intervals.

## Reaction correlations

R2/R4/R5 below are generated from the current selected JSON. It does not serialize fixed R1/R3; those rows and the reaction equations come from the retained [chemistry declaration](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/blob/30ce082/data/reference/MEA/manifests/chemical_reaction_source_contract.json), including its stored aqueous-molality offsets.

::: {.parameter-table .summary-table}
| Reaction | $A$ (1) | $B$ (K) | $C$ (1) | $D$ (K⁻¹) | $\Delta$ (1) | Input owner |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| R1 · 2 H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">132.9</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−1.345e+04</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−22.48</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">8.033</span> | Fixed chemistry |
| R2 · CO₂ + 2 H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + H₃O⁺ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">234.9</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−1.193e+04</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−36.78</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0</span> | — | Selected JSON |
| R3 · HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">216.0</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−1.243e+04</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−35.48</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">4.017</span> | Fixed chemistry |
| R4 · MEACOO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + MEA | <span class="evidence-2" title="">2.151</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−1545</span> | — | — | — | Selected JSON |
:::

R5 uses a base-10 logarithm and different coefficient units:

::: {.parameter-table .summary-table}
| Reaction | $A$ (K) | $B$ (1) | $C$ (K⁻¹) | Input owner |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| R5 · MEAH⁺ + H₂O ⇌ MEA + H₃O⁺ | <span class="evidence-2" title="">3354</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">−1.281</span> | <span class="evidence-2" title="">0.0004277</span> | Selected JSON |
:::

For R1–R3, $\ln K=A+B/T+C\ln T+DT+\Delta$; R2 already includes the conversion in $A$ and has no separate offset. For R4, $\ln K=A+B/T$. For R5, $-\log_{10}K=A/T+B+CT$. The displayed layouts therefore give $B$ in K for R1–R4 and $A$ in K for R5; $D$ for R1–R3 and $C$ for R5 are in K⁻¹. Other coefficients are dimensionless. R2/R5 include the fitted pivot-preserving enthalpy shifts at 313.15 K; R5 also varies its unshifted source A. The displayed reaction coefficients include these transformations and are not independent fitted coordinates or new source measurements.

## Integral heat of absorption {#heat-of-absorption}

The [22 retained heat rows](results/a7-paper-evidence/heat.csv) comprise the fitted and non-fitted comparisons below. Eight Vinjarapu rows at 313.15 K and 1.734 MPa enter the objective; 14 Arcis rows at 322.5 K are non-fitted predictions at their source pressures. Heat is the integral finite-addition enthalpy from zero carbon. Negative heat denotes exothermic absorption.

![A7 integral heat of absorption. Open markers are observations; + markers are calculated at measured states. Vinjarapu is fitted and Arcis is a non-fitted prediction.](figures/a7_regression_overview/output/heat-of-absorption.svg){#fig-heat}

Root-mean-square error (RMSE) and calculated-minus-observed bias are in kJ/mol CO₂.

## Density {#density-and-heat-capacity}

The [210 retained densities](results/a7-paper-evidence/density.csv) are native equation-of-state predictions, with no empirical volume translation. The objective contains 47 loaded and five CO₂-free densities. Source pressures remain the retained assumptions, including 0.100 MPa where unreported. The other retained rows preserve their non-fitted roles and exclusions.

![A7 fitted loaded-density errors, normalized by each row’s retained scale. Dashed lines are the row-specific 2s limits after normalization; the three named failures are at 353.15 K. These scales are not uniformly measured uncertainties.](figures/a7_regression_overview/output/loaded-density-errors.svg){#fig-density}

Three fitted loaded densities at 353.15 K fall outside their $2s$ limits (−2.28$s$, −2.06$s$, −2.43$s$). These three rows are underpredicted by 4.2–5.5 kg/m³ (0.40–0.53%). The source-uncertainty discussion and the five excluded Amundsen rows are on the [A7 page](joint-recalibration/index.qmd).
